## Purpose

This SOP establishes the minimum standards for field documentation in
the EA Program. Complete, legible, and contemporaneous field notes are
the foundation of defensible environmental data [@kanare1985]. Notes
recorded in the field cannot be reconstructed later from memory; what
is not written down at the time is effectively lost. This SOP ensures
that every field visit produces a record sufficient for another trained
researcher to understand what was done, where, when, by whom, and under
what conditions.

For laboratory notebook requirements, see
[SOP-L010 Laboratory Notebook Recording](../lab_sops/SOP-L010-lab-notebook-recording.qmd).


## Scope

- **Applies to:** All EA Program field activities, including sampling,
  sensor deployment and retrieval, site reconnaissance, equipment
  installation, and monitoring visits.
- **Does not apply to:** Laboratory work or purely digital data
  collection on tablets and phones (though digital entries should
  follow the same content standards described here).
- **Location:** All EA Program field sites.


## Responsibilities

| Role                | Responsibility                                        |
|:--------------------|:------------------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI              | Set documentation standards; review notebooks periodically |
| Field Lead          | Ensure all team members record required entries        |
| All Field Personnel | Maintain a field notebook per this SOP                |
| New Students        | Read this SOP before their first field outing          |


## Definitions

- **Chain of custody (COC):** A documented record of sample possession
  at every transfer point from collection to laboratory analysis; the
  COC form number must be cross-referenced in the field notebook entry
  for the corresponding samples.
- **Contemporaneous record:** An entry made at the time the observation
  or action occurs, not reconstructed from memory afterward; the
  defining characteristic of a legally defensible field or laboratory
  record [@kanare1985].
- **Deviation:** Any departure from a written SOP during field
  activities; must be recorded in the notebook with the reason for the
  deviation and an assessment of its potential effect on data quality.
- **Field notebook:** A bound, weather-resistant notebook with
  numbered pages used to record all field observations, measurements,
  and activities; the primary raw-data record for a field project
  [@kanare1985].
- **Good Documentation Practice (GDP):** A set of principles for
  creating accurate, legible, contemporaneous, original, and
  attributable records; the foundation of data integrity in regulated
  and research laboratories [@broman2018].
- **Header block:** A standardized set of fields (date, time, site,
  personnel, weather, purpose, SOPs in use) recorded at the top of
  each field visit entry before any observations or data are logged.
- **Rite in the Rain:** A brand of field notebook and paper products
  printed on water-resistant stock that can be written on with
  ballpoint or mechanical pencil even in rain; the preferred notebook
  format for EA Program field work.
- **Sample ID:** A unique alphanumeric code assigned to each sample
  at the moment of collection, cross-referencing the field notebook,
  sample label, COC form, and laboratory data file.
- **Tare mass:** Not applicable in field notebooks -- see
  [SOP-L400 Soil Moisture](../lab_sops/SOP-L400-soil-moisture.qmd).
- **Time stamp:** The date and time of a discrete field action,
  recorded in the notebook at the moment of the action; use ISO 8601
  format (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM) or a consistent AM/PM scheme throughout
  the notebook.


## Notebook Selection and Preparation

### Acceptable Notebooks

Use a bound, weather-resistant field notebook with numbered pages.
Acceptable options include:

- Rite in the Rain (top-spiral or side-spiral, any size)
- Any hardbound notebook with numbered pages (if weather protection is
  not required for the site)

Do **not** use loose-leaf paper, spiral notebooks with perforated
pages, or sticky notes for primary field records [@kanare1985].

### Front Matter

On the inside front cover or first page of a new notebook, record:

- Your name, phone number, and email
- "If found, please return to: EA Program, Pomona College, SGM 133"
- Project name(s)
- Date the notebook was put into service

### Page Numbering

If pages are not pre-numbered, number them in ink before going to the
field. Never remove pages from a field notebook.


## Required Entries for Every Field Visit

Every field visit entry must begin with the following header
information. Write it before you do anything else on site.

### Header Block

Record at the top of a new page or clearly separated section:

| Field               | Example                                       |
|:--------------------|:----------------------------------------------|
| Date                | 2026-05-18 (ISO format: YYYY-MM-DD)           |
| Time of arrival     | 08:15 PST                                     |
| Site name / ID      | Bernard Field Station, Plot BFS-03            |
| GPS coordinates     | 34.0975 N, 117.7125 W (WGS84)                |
| Personnel present   | M. Los Huertos, J. Smith                      |
| Weather conditions  | Clear, ~25 °C, light wind from W, no recent rain |
| Purpose of visit    | Soil sampling for CN analysis; sensor download |
| SOPs in use         | F400, F401, F510                              |

### Time Stamps

Record the time of every discrete action: sample collection,
instrument reading, equipment start/stop, calibration check, photo
taken. Use 24-hour format or AM/PM consistently throughout the
notebook [@broman2018].

### Site Observations

Before beginning work, note anything relevant:

- Visible changes since the last visit (new construction, vegetation
  removal, standing water, animal activity, vandalism, equipment
  condition)
- Odors or visual indicators of contamination
- Land use activities in progress nearby (mowing, irrigation,
  construction)

### Sample and Measurement Records

For each sample collected or measurement taken, record at minimum:

- Sample ID (use the project's established naming convention)
- Time of collection or measurement
- Location (plot, transect position, depth, or other descriptor)
- Value or description (e.g., "pH = 7.2," "soil moist, dark brown,
  loamy texture")
- Preservation method applied (e.g., "filtered, acidified with
  HNO~3~ to pH < 2")
- Container type and label verification

::: {.callout-tip}
### Write More Than You Think You Need
Include observations that seem obvious at the time. "Soil was
saturated and smelled of sulfide" or "sensor housing had a spider web
across the inlet" may be critical for interpreting data months later
[@kanare1985].
:::

### Equipment and Instrument Notes

Record for every instrument used:

- Instrument ID (serial number or lab asset tag)
- Calibration status (date of last calibration; field check performed?)
- Settings (logging interval, flow rate, method name)
- Any malfunctions, error messages, or anomalies

### Deviations from SOPs

If you deviate from the standard procedure for any reason, record:

- What you did differently and why
- Whether the deviation may affect data quality
- Who authorized the deviation (if applicable)

### Departure

Before leaving the site, record:

- Time of departure
- Summary of work completed and any work left undone
- Disposition of samples (e.g., "cooler with ice, to lab by 12:00")
- Any follow-up actions needed


## Sketches and Diagrams

A simple sketch is often more informative than a paragraph of text
[@kanare1985]. Include sketches of:

- Site layout showing sampling locations, landmarks, and compass
  orientation
- Equipment placement (sensor positions, transect layout, plot
  boundaries)
- Anything unusual (erosion features, spill boundaries, wildlife
  sightings relevant to the study)

Label all sketches with a north arrow, approximate scale, date, and
your initials.


## Photographs

### When to Photograph

- At the start of every visit: a general site photo showing conditions
- Each sampling location before and after sampling
- Equipment installations and sensor positions
- Anything unusual or noteworthy (damage, contamination indicators,
  unexpected conditions)
- Calibration setups

### Photo Naming and Logging

Record in the notebook the photo number or filename and a brief
description for every photo taken:

> "Photo IMG\_4231: Plot BFS-03 looking NE, pre-sampling, 08:22"

Transfer photos to the project folder within 48 hours and rename using
the convention:

`YYYY-MM-DD_SiteID_Description_PhotoNumber.jpg`

Back up photos to the project GitHub repository or shared drive
[@broman2018].


## Corrections and Errors

- Never erase, white-out, or obliterate an entry.
- To correct an error, draw a single line through the incorrect text
  so it remains legible. Write the correction nearby and initial and
  date the change.
- If you skip a page or leave blank space, draw a diagonal line
  through the unused area and initial it to prevent later additions
  [@kanare1985].


## Chain of Custody

When samples will be submitted to an analytical laboratory (internal
or external), complete a Chain of Custody (COC) form. The COC must
accompany the samples and include:

- Project name and PI
- Sample IDs matching the field notebook entries
- Date and time of collection
- Number and type of containers
- Analyses requested
- Preservatives applied
- Signatures at each transfer (field to transport, transport to lab)

Record the COC form number in the field notebook entry for
cross-reference. See
[SOP-F008 Sample Labeling, COC, and Transport](SOP-F008-sample-labeling-coc-transport.qmd)
for the full chain-of-custody procedure.


## Notebook Archiving

- At the end of a field season or project, submit completed notebooks
  to the PI for archiving.
- Notebooks are stored in labeled binders in SGM 133 and must be
  retained for a minimum of 5 years after project completion.
- Transcribe key data from notebooks to digital spreadsheets within
  48 hours of each field visit, following the tidy data principles in
  @broman2018. Flag any discrepancies between the notebook and the
  digital record and resolve them with the field lead.

## Training Record

Before conducting any field work independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Set up a field notebook with correct front matter
3. Complete a practice header block entry under supervision
4. Demonstrate correct error-correction technique (single-line
   strikethrough, initials, date)
5. Be signed off by the PI or field lead
